title: Host Header Injection and Cache Poisoning Static Analysis Rules

rules.name: Host header injection in redirect or link construction
rules.description: Trusting raw Host or X-Forwarded-Host request headers in Python web handlers to construct password-reset links or redirects without allowlist validation allows host header injection and cache poisoning.
rules.remediation_example: host = request.headers.get('host'); if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS: raise BadRequest()  # validate against strict allowlist

rules.name: Unkeyed cache and proxy header exposure
rules.description: Web surface check for unkeyed cache/proxy headers (X-Cache, CF-Cache-Status, Age, Via) combined with missing Vary headers or reflected X-Forwarded-Host values.
rules.remediation_example: response.headers['Vary'] = 'Host, Accept-Encoding'  # ensure upstream caches key on the Host header

rules.name: Host header password reset poisoning via email
rules.description: Password reset email template interpolates raw Host header into password reset URL, allowing attackers to trigger password resets that send reset tokens to attacker-controlled domains.
rules.remediation_example: reset_url = f'{SERVER_BASE_URL}/reset?token={token}'  # use fixed server base URL rather than request Host
